entries.title: arXiv 2608.05158: Circuit-Anchored Evolution (CAE) — Safety Preserved During LLM Self-Evolution with <2% of Features Locked
entries.summary: CAE identifies a tiny 'safety circuit' (< 2% of model features) that causally mediates safety behaviors, anchors it during self-evolution within a small displacement bound, and substantially outperforms reward-based safety constraints across 3 model families — preventing models from misevolving into capable-but-unsafe systems analogous to how Hox genes constrain biological evolution.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05563: PoisonedEvolution — Trajectory Poisoning Embeds Target Behaviors in 91% of Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems with Only 10% Attacker Support
entries.summary: A black-box attacker who can inspect a target skill and contribute bounded evidence (but not edit the skill bank) embeds malicious behaviors in 546/600 trials (91% SER) across six LLM evolvers, exploiting 'attribution' — causal framing, recurrence, and domain alignment — as the bottleneck in self-evolving skill promotion; the attack transfers across evolution architectures at 61.5% SER.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05223: Malicious Skill Files in Coding Agents — Gemini CLI Exploited in 96% of Runs, Safety Recognition in Only 2%
entries.summary: A benchmark of 2,826 adversarially synthesized skill files (mapping to 11 MITRE ATT&CK tactics) run across enterprise-grade agents finds Gemini CLI is exploited in 95.5–96.1% of runs and Qwen Code in 71.6–74.0%, with safety recognition occurring in only 1.99% of runs, establishing the agent skills interface as a critical attack surface requiring assessment before enterprise adoption.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05210: Multi-Turn AI Image Generation Completes 80%+ of Hateful Visual Story Configurations — Dedicated Safety Models Catch Only 35%
entries.summary: Every frontier T2I model tested (including Gemini and GPT-Image) completes over 80% of hateful multi-turn visual story sequences (best reaching 99%), while dedicated safety models achieve at most 34.9% recall, revealing a fundamental group-level safety gap as image generation shifts from isolated outputs to coherent narratives and requiring stateful rather than per-image moderation.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05409: Grammatical Mood Creates a Broadly Applicable Jailbreak Across 16 LLMs Up to 70B Parameters
entries.summary: Non-imperative syntactic forms (past tense, subjunctive, etc.) systematically bypass safety alignment in 16 models up to 70B parameters; causal mediation analysis traces the vulnerability to refusal being partially conditioned on upstream syntactic rather than semantic features, and increasing syntactic diversity in post-training data substantially mitigates it.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05578: AMS — Activation-Space Scanner Detects Safety Training Modifications Across 4 LLM Architecture Families, But Behavioral-Only Modifications Remain Undetectable
entries.summary: AMS measures geometric structure in safety-relevant activation space and identifies a four-class taxonomy of safety modifications (training removal, weight-orthogonalization abliteration, rotation-without-collapse, behavioral fine-tuning), achieving 71% leave-one-out accuracy across 14 configurations on Llama, Gemma, Qwen, and Mistral; behavioral-only modifications are documented as an undetectable failure mode.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05909: MMAligner (CCS 2026) — Representation Calibration Raises MLLM Refusal Rate on Unsafe Multimodal Inputs to 99% with <2% Utility Loss
entries.summary: MMAligner diagnoses multimodal safety failures as representation misalignment (not absent safety capability) and calibrates unsafe multimodal representations back into the pre-existing refusal region using hard/soft bounds and a preservation objective, achieving 99% refusal on unsafe multimodal inputs with under 2% utility degradation across multiple open-source MLLMs.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.05659: ARIA (ASE 2026) — Automated Red-Teaming Framework Backdoors Customized Coding LLMs with 94.5% Success Rate and Up to 100% Platform-Side Evasion
entries.summary: ARIA uses an attacker LLM to iteratively craft covert backdoored instructions for task-specific coding LLMs across stealthiness, utility, and effectiveness dimensions, achieving a 0.945 attack success rate and false-negative rates up to 1.000 against platform- and user-side detection while remaining robust to existing defenses across four frontier models.

entries.title: "Great American AI Act" Stalls in US House Over State Preemption Clause — 14+ State AI Frameworks Now Operative
entries.summary: After passing the Senate in late June, the US federal AI bill has stalled in the House over a preemption clause that would override state AI laws, leaving over 14 different state-level AI frameworks (California, Colorado, Texas, Illinois, etc.) as the operative US compliance reality and forcing companies to geo-fence features or adopt the strictest state standard nationally.

entries.title: EU AI Office Publishes First List of 8 Frontier Foundation Models Above 10^25 FLOPs Threshold — Monthly Systemic Risk Evaluations Now Required
entries.summary: The EU AI Office identified 8 foundation models exceeding the 10^25 FLOPs training threshold under the AI Act's GPAI systemic risk framework (which became enforceable August 2), requiring their providers to submit monthly systemic risk evaluations; violations face fines up to €15M or 3% of global annual revenue.

entries.title: UK AI Regulation and Safety Bill Clears House of Commons — Royal Assent Expected by October
entries.summary: The UK AI Regulation and Safety Bill passed the House of Commons this week, placing the UK on track for binding statutory AI governance with Royal Assent expected by October 2026, complementing the EU AI Act's August 2 enforcement activation.

entries.title: Federal Reprimand Issued Over Medicare AI Prior-Authorization Pilot — Automated Denials Without Clinical Oversight or Appeal Pathways
entries.summary: A federal reprimand was issued following failures in Medicare's AI-driven prior-authorization pilot that produced automated delays and disputed denials without adequate clinical oversight or appeal pathways, establishing a concrete enforcement precedent for any healthcare organization using AI in utilization management or claims adjudication.

entries.title: Amazon Shuts Down KiroRank AI Coding Leaderboard After Employees Game the System
entries.summary: Amazon shut down KiroRank, an internal leaderboard for its Kiro agentic AI coding platform, after employees discovered ways to manipulate the ranking system, illustrating the governance risk of misaligned metrics in enterprise AI adoption programs and the inadequacy of performance proxies as behavioral controls.

entries.title: Mistral Releases Shieldstral — Apache 2.0 Open-Weight Multimodal Content Moderation Model with Policy-as-Plain-Language Interface
entries.summary: Mistral's Shieldstral allows enterprises to define safety policies as natural-language questions at inference time without retraining, returning calibrated safety scores for text, images, and combined inputs across prompt classification, response moderation, and refusal detection — shifting content moderation governance in-house with an open-weight model.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Mistral's Open-Weight Safety Classifier

entries.title: Hallucinated AI Security Intelligence Report Brands Startup as Chinese Spy Front, Causing Global Domain Block
entries.summary: An AI Failure Index case documents an LLM-assisted security threat report that falsely branded a startup as a Chinese spy front without factual basis; published without expert review, it caused global domain blocks, illustrating direct third-party harm liability when human fact-checking is absent from AI-assisted security intelligence products.
